data.description:
Determine why llama-server (Qwen3 child on port 58113) becomes unresponsive. Evidence from /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log:

1. slot_save failed slot=0/1/2 error=PoolTimeout/PoolTimeout with elapsed up to 60.0s, recurring throughout the day — including when busy shows active_queries: 0, local_active_queries: 0, slot_busy: false (idle slots still timing out).
2. Stream error: provider=local model=Qwen3 error=OSError at 15:08:14-15:08:16 (3 sessions: audit-SA-..., audit-AH-..., herdr-...): 'Local stream error (OSError); llama-server may be unhealthy'.
3. status_request lines intermittently show llama_server_running=false while local streams still complete.

Proxy and llama-server run on the same machine (192.168.0.199 is this host), so 'network errors' is not a valid explanation. Need to investigate llama-server health directly: process state, GPU memory/utilization, llama-server logs, load at failure timestamps.
data.title: Investigate llama-server health: slot_save PoolTimeouts and OSError stream errors

data.author: pi
data.comment: Both fix children complete and pushed to dev: LP-0MTDH2Q8C001WEGU (cb0c199) routes availability checks to the child port + skips on lease-hold; LP-0MTDH2U6V0062TUF (a60b95f) gives the availability check a dedicated 2s-timeout client. Full suite green (2439 passed via test-skill runner). Audit findings are 24 pre-existing ruff issues in unrelated files (context-distribution scripts, LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE scope) — none in changed files. Parent advanced to in_review.
